title: Some Pixel Watch 5 users are missing a Google Home feature older models already have
summary: Live view works on older Pixel Watches, making this glitch all the more puzzling.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel Watch 5 owners can’t view live camera feeds in Google Home. The feature still works on older Pixel Watches and unaffected Watch 5 units. Google’s troubleshooting steps and a replacement watch reportedly failed to resolve it. A new smartwatch shouldn’t make you miss the one it replaced. Yet barely a month into the Pixel Watch 5 ‘s life, some early owners are discovering that their older Google watches can do something the latest model cannot: show live camera feeds in the Google Home app. Several reports on Reddit and the Pixel Watch Community describe what happens when affected users select a camera in the Home app: Instead of loading the video, the watch displays a “Control more features on your phone” message and an “Open on phone” button. body: Working from home has its perks, the biggest being avoiding a hectic morning commute. That means that my car spends most of the week sitting in the driveway. I mostly just use it for the occasional weekend road trip, so I’ve never been able to justify upgrading my vehicle to a newer model with Android Auto support. title: Google Photos just halved the time you have to rescue trashed pictures
summary: Google Photos is starting to clear your trash after 30 days, not 60.
body: TL;DR Last month we spotted Google Photos preparing to implement a new 30-day retention limit on deleted pics. A few days ago, Google updated its Photos support docs to reference the new 30-day policy. Now Android users are also starting to get notifications within the app. How much effort do you put into to curating your photographs? When you’ve got a giant bucket of Google One storage to fill up, some users will just save every snapshot they ever take. Even when you have all the space in the world, there’s a lot to be said for weeding out the pics you definitely don’t want. But what if you end up second-guessing yourself? Maybe that questionable pic is worth keeping, after all? Hopefully you make up your mind soon, because Google Photos is slashing your restore window in half for trashed pics. So far, if you’ve backed up an image with Google Photos, then moved that pic to the trash, you’d get a 60-day grace period before it was deleted for good. For pics that are just stored locally on a device, you’ve only had 30 days.
